description: INT-004, canon §7: a viewer touches the mouse and he freezes — and a mouse that does not bolt is a mouse the cat can actually reach. LOCAL: the cat's path is local (NPC-004), so where he is when this fires differs per client and this can never touch the shared schedule. The event sets up the BEAT — the mouse holds, the cat comes — and the cat's controller owns the SEQUENCE inside it (pounce, bat, release, the mouse away to the hole, a paw washed about it), because how long the approach takes is a distance across a room, not a timestamp. `npc/cat/hunt` refuses when there is no prey out, so a fire that arrives with him in the wall plays nothing rather than a cat stalking an empty floor. ★ IT CLAIMS NO EXCLUSIVE CHANNEL, AND THAT IS THE POINT: `exclusive` DROPS rather than queues, and the only time the mouse is tappable at all is while an ambient beat has him out of the wall — so an event exclusive on `mouse` could be refused by the very errand that made the tap possible. Measured: a press during mouse_errand fired nothing and logged nothing at all. The remaining risk is a scheduled beat commanding him mid-freeze, which the controller's own refusals already handle. The hold is 18–26 s and NOT the 9–15 s it was first authored at: measured, the cat took most of twenty seconds to cross the room and the freeze expired with him 0.61 m away, so the beat ended in the mouse simply walking off before anything happened. It is an upper bound rather than a duration — the cat's arrival releases him (the controller's bat-and-release), so the number only has to outlast the walk.
